EOAS5000.d: An introduction to the fundamentals of physical, chemical, geological, geochemical, and biological oceanography. It unveils the mystery of the oceans including the formation of the continents, oceanic circulation, and formation of precious minerals in the deep oceans; discovers ocean resources from phytoplankton to fish. The course will lay the foundation for sustainable use of the oceans and discuss human threats such as global warming, overfishing, and coastal pollution.
cl: Describe ocean sciences from interdisciplinary perspectives including physics, chemistry, biology, and geology.
Analyze environmental and earth system problems based on fundamental scientific principles and by applying interdisciplinary skill and knowledge.
Communicate problem solutions using correct oceanographic terminology in English.

EOAS5001.d: This course introduces the Earth surface system in the watershed. It provides fundamental knowledge, theory, and methodology for the Earth surface processes that link with atmosphere and coastal ocean. The course content provides not only basic training on the Earth surface processes but also cross-interdisciplinary training on the interactions between physical and biogeochemical processes among land, sea, and air. We aim to train the students to possess interdisciplinary and comprehensive skills to tackle the challenges in the changing Earth system.
cl: Build fundamental knowledge and theory of physics and biogeochemistry in the Earth surface processes.
Analyze problems in the Earth surface processes based on fundamental scientific principles and by applying interdisciplinary skill and knowledge.
Describe Earth surface sciences from interdisciplinary perspectives including physics, chemistry, biology andgeology.
Develop an interdisciplinary scientific understanding of the land-ocean-atmosphere system.
Acquire methodology and skills to conduct the Earth surface processes study.
Communicate problem solutions using correct Earth surface science terminology in English.

2520.d: This course introduces the Earth surface hydrodynamics, biogeochemical cycles, sediment and climate processes focusing on the river basin and watershed that link with atmosphere, river water, soil, vegetation, landscape, impact of humans, submarine groundwater discharge and ocean for the modification of Earth system.

EOAS5002.d: This course presents fundamental geophysical fluid dynamics in the ocean and atmosphere system by introducing governing concepts and principles in ocean and atmospheric circulation as well as the exchanges of buoyancy, energy and momentum fluxes in the interface between air and sea.
cl: Analyze problems in coupled atmosphere and ocean system based on fundamental scientific principles and by applying interdisciplinary skill and knowledge.
Describe atmosphere and ocean dynamics from perspectives including physics, mathematics and geophysical fluid dynamics.
Communicate problem solutions using correct terminology of atmosphere and ocean dynamics in English.

EOAS5003.d: The biogeochemical cycle in the ocean is not only governed by the chemical and biological processes, but also regulated critically by the physical processes in the ocean. The topics of this course cover ocean circulation and biogeochemical dynamics, marine phytoplankton and zooplankton, biogeochemical response to circulation dynamics in the ocean.
cl: Analyze problems in coupled physical and biogeochemical processes in the ocean based on fundamental scientific principles and by applying interdisciplinary skill and knowledge.
Describe biophysical processes in the ocean from interdisciplinary perspectives including physics, chemistry and biology.
Communicate problem solutions using correct interdisciplinary oceanography terminology in English.

EOAS5004.d: The course covers major processes and interactions of Earth system components and introduces the related numerical modeling concepts and techniques. It provides hands-on modeling projects to explore ideas of designing, constructing, and applying models to test hypotheses and enhance understanding of the Earth system processes and their response and feedback to the climate.
cl: Identify the core ideas and concepts of the interdisciplinary earth system science.
Understand basic numerical methods and their application in studying earth system processes.
Develop critical thinking skills to conduct investigative research in different components of the earth system.
Apply numerical modeling concepts and quantitative methods to analyze problems in the earth system.
Translate effectively fundamental knowledge into the earth and environmental science practice in relevant academic and engineering fields.

EOAS5005.d: This course introduces the fundamental principles and processes that govern the Earth’s atmosphere, covering a broad range of topics including atmospheric thermodynamics, radiative transfer, cloud formation, atmospheric circulation, weather systems, and climate variability. These core concepts provide the foundation for understanding the role of the atmosphere in the global energy and water cycles. The course also synthesizes these topics within the context of pressing societal challenges such as extreme weather events, air pollution, and climate change.
cl: Develop a foundational understanding of the key physical principles and processes governing the Earth's atmosphere.
Build basic knowledge of the atmosphere’s role in the Earth’s energy balance and hydrological cycle.
Apply fundamental physical laws to interpret and explain weather and climate phenomena.

2520.d: This course introduces the fundamental principles that govern the physical and chemical processes in the atmosphere, including the thermodynamics of dry and moist air, radiative transfer, important trace gases and aerosols, and essential aspects of atmospheric circulation, etc. These fundamental principles form the basis of understanding the role of atmosphere in the global energy, water and carbon cycles, and the interaction between the atmosphere and other components of the Earth system. This course also provides a synthesis of these topics in the context of critical issues that are affecting human society such as extreme weather events, air pollution, and climate change.

EOAS5006.d: This course provides fundamental knowledge of how carbon flows through the land-ocean-atmosphere continuum and how carbon interacts with the cycling of water and other essential biogeochemical elements to regulate the Earth’s climate. It provides insight into human activities altering the carbon cycle, the global climate, and ecosystem dynamics. It also explores nature-based solutions or eco-engineering strategies for achieving carbon neutrality and mitigating adverse climate and ecosystem changes.
cl: Develop interdisciplinary concepts and knowledge in the global carbon cycle and its crucial role in regulating Earth’s climate.
Acquire foundational knowledge and theories of carbon and other essential biogeochemical cycles, and understand how they will both affect and respond to global changes and human activities.
Appreciate the latest research trend and state-of-the-art techniques in achieving carbon neutralization and mitigating adverse climate and ecosystem changes.
Build fundamental knowledge and analytical skills useful in natural sciences in general.

EOAS5007.d: This course addresses foundational theories, knowledge, and current challenges within the broad and interdisciplinary field of watershed biogeochemistry, focusing on the biogeochemical, hydrological, and ecological connections across the land-air-water continuum in watersheds. General themes will be explored through lectures on basic theories and discussions of recent literature. More specific questions and methodological approaches will be introduced using hands-on practices and excursions to field sites. This course will enhance students' understanding of water, carbon, and nutrient cycling along the terrestrial-aquatic interface.

2520.d: This course focuses on the biogeochemical, hydrological, and ecological connections across the land-air-water continuum in watersheds. Specific topics include 1) an overview of watershed biogeochemical cycles, 2) land-air exchanges of carbon, water, and energy, 3) nutrient cycles in land and waters, 4) biogeochemical cycling in groundwater, and 5) watershed biogeochemistry in climate change.

EOAS5008.d: This course is designed to provide postgraduate students with the opportunity to practice speaking and presenting their research in front of scientific audiences. Students will select research topics and organize presentations within the interdisciplinary studies of ocean-atmosphere-land interactions for faculty and other students.

EOAS5009.d: This course explores the sources, impacts, and control measures for different types of environmental pollutants, covering topics such as air pollutants, drinking water pollutants, and soil pollution (including organic pollutants and heavy metals), etc. Students will gain the knowledge and skills necessary to design and implement effective pollution control measures for diverse environmental challenges.
cl: Describe key environmental pollution issues and their associated risks.
Apply analytical techniques to monitor and predict environmental pollution scenarios.
Design appropriate control and mitigation strategies for various environmental pollutants.
Differentiate between emission sources and assess corresponding control measures.
Develop and apply analytical reasoning to address interdisciplinary problems in atmospheric and environmental sciences.

EOAS5010.d: This is a seminar style course discussing selected topics in contemporary global environmental challenges, covering scientific understanding, technological and policy solutions. Cutting-edge high-impact interdisciplinary publications in the nexus of earth sciences and sustainability literature, reports, classical textbook chapters, policy documents, etc. will be provided for students to read before the class for in-class discussions. The course will cover topics including the planetary boundary framework, human-earth complex systems, trans-environmental media reactive nitrogen pollution, land use change, biodiversity loss, transboundary air pollution, co-mitigation of air pollution and climate change, international trade and environmental justice, and application of AI to earth sciences.
cl: Acquire fundamental knowledge about the sciences of global environmental challenges, potential technical solutions and environmental policy instruments.
Appreciate frontier interdisciplinary high-impact research in the nexus of earth sciences, environmental management and sustainability sciences and incorporate it into graduate research design.
Evaluate state-of-the-art modeling/observation/AI approaches for characterizing sources and transformation of environmental pollution and their interactions with human society.
Develop analytical interdisciplinary concepts, knowledge and skills for approaching human impacts on earth systems useful for earth science and interdisciplinary research.
Substantially improve English reading and critical thinking skills after digesting a wide range of reading materials.
Strengthen communication, collaboration and presentation skills after engaging in frequent small group discussions and debates.

EOAS6000.d: Selected topics of current interest in emerging areas and not covered by existing courses. May be repeated for credit if different topics are covered. May be graded by letter or P/F for different offerings.
cl: Develop interdisciplinary concepts and knowledge in the chosen topics in Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences
Acquire foundational knowledge and theories of the chosen topics
Appreciate the latest research trend and state-of-the-art techniques in the chosen topics
Build fundamental knowledge and analytical skills useful in natural sciences in general

EOAS6900.d: Study on selected topics in the Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences under the supervision of a faculty member.
cl:
Demonstrate mastery of the knowledge and skills in the selected topics related to the Earth, Ocean, and 
Atmospheric Sciences (EOAS).
Apply an interdisciplinary approach in examining the selected topics.
Critically evaluate different aspects of the selected topics.
Communicate findings effectively in written reports.

EOAS6990.d: Master's thesis research supervised by co-advisors from different disciplines. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.
cl: Design, develop and conduct cross-disciplinary research in Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric System.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.

EOAS7990.d: Original and independent doctoral thesis research supervised by co-advisors from different disciplines. A successful defense of the thesis leads to the grade Pass. No course credit is assigned.
cl: Design, develop and conduct cross-disciplinary research in Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric System.
Communicate research findings effectively in written and oral presentations.
